steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: An interest rate is the cost of borrowing or the reward for saving, expressed as a percentage of the amount. | Key Fact: Higher interest rates: encourage saving (better returns), discourage borrowing (more expensive loans), reduce spending (mortgages cost more, less disposable income), and reduce business investment (borrowing costs rise). | Key Fact: Lower interest rates: discourage saving, encourage borrowing and spending, stimulate investment, and can lead to inflation if demand grows too fast. | Key Fact: The Bank of England sets the base interest rate to control inflation — raising rates to cool the economy, lowering to stimulate it.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain how a rise in interest rates affects consumers' decisions to save, borrow, and spend. | Explain how a fall in interest rates might affect a firm's decision to invest in new equipment. | Evaluate whether the Bank of England should raise interest rates when inflation is rising.
